evidence.quote: It all began, old Ammi said, with the meteorite.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator identifies the meteorite's fall as the origin of all the strange events.

evidence.quote: And by night all Arkham had heard of the great rock that fell out of the sky and bedded itself in the ground beside the well at the Nahum Gardner place.
evidence.paraphrase: A rock arrives from the sky and embeds itself in the ground near the farm's well.

evidence.quote: It had acted quite unbelievably in that well-ordered laboratory; doing nothing at all and showing no occluded gases when heated on charcoal, being wholly negative in the borax bead, and soon proving itself absolutely non-volatile at any producible temperature, including that of the oxy-hydrogen blowpipe.
evidence.paraphrase: Laboratory tests on the meteorite fragment describe its anomalous physical and chemical behavior.

evidence.quote: when upon heating before the spectroscope it displayed shining bands unlike any known colours of the normal spectrum there was much breathless talk of new elements, bizarre optical properties, and other things which puzzled men of science are wont to say when faced by the unknown.
evidence.paraphrase: Scientists use spectroscopy on the fragment and find an unknown spectrum, prompting speculation about new elements.

evidence.quote: There were ammonia and caustic soda, alcohol and ether, nauseous carbon disulphide and a dozen others; but although the weight grew steadily less as time passed, and the fragment seemed to be slightly cooling, there was no change in the solvents to show that they had attacked the substance at all.
evidence.paraphrase: The scientists systematically test many solvents on the fragment, none of which affect it.

evidence.quote: It was nothing of this earth, but a piece of the great outside; and as such dowered with outside properties and obedient to outside laws.
evidence.paraphrase: The scientists conclude the substance is not earthly and obeys laws foreign to earth.

evidence.quote: The colour, which resembled some of the bands in the meteor's strange spectrum, was almost impossible to describe; and it was only by analogy that they called it colour at all.
evidence.paraphrase: A coloured globule inside the meteorite has a colour that cannot be properly described, only called colour by analogy.

evidence.quote: The fruit was growing to phenomenal size and unwonted gloss, and in such abundance that extra barrels were ordered to handle the future crop. But with the ripening came sore disappointment, for of all that gorgeous array of specious lusciousness not one single jot was fit to eat.
evidence.paraphrase: The crops grow abnormally large and glossy but become inedible after the meteorite's arrival.

evidence.quote: All the orchard trees blossomed forth in strange colours, and through the stony soil of the yard and adjacent pasturage there sprang up a bizarre growth which only a botanist could connect with the proper flora of the region.
evidence.paraphrase: The vegetation develops strange, unnatural colours and bizarre growth around the farm.

evidence.quote: The swine began growing grey and brittle and falling to pieces before they died, and their eyes and muzzles developed singular alterations.
evidence.paraphrase: The livestock undergo grotesque physical changes, greying and disintegrating before death.

evidence.quote: In her raving there was not a single specific noun, but only verbs and pronouns. Things moved and changed and fluttered, and ears tingled to impulses which were not wholly sounds. Something was taken away\u2014she was being drained of something
evidence.paraphrase: Mrs. Gardner goes mad, describing indescribable things and feeling drained of something.

evidence.quote: Under the spectroscope both samples gave off an unknown spectrum, in which many of the baffling bands were precisely like those which the strange meteor had yielded in the previous year. The property of emitting this spectrum vanished in a month, the dust thereafter consisting mainly of alkaline phosphates and carbonates.
evidence.paraphrase: Later spectroscopic analysis of dust samples matches the meteor's earlier unknown spectrum, which fades in a month.

evidence.quote: Merwin and Zenas were both there, in part, though the vestiges were mainly skeletal. There were also a small deer and a large dog in about the same state, and a number of bones of smaller animals.
evidence.paraphrase: The remains of the missing boys and animals are found reduced to bones in the well.

evidence.quote: there burst up from that doomed and accursed farm a gleamingly eruptive cataclysm of unnatural sparks and substance; blurring the glance of the few who saw it, and sending forth to the zenith a bombarding cloudburst of such coloured and fantastic fragments as our universe must needs disown.
evidence.paraphrase: The farm erupts in a cataclysmic burst of unnatural coloured substance shooting into the sky.

evidence.quote: Then without warning the hideous thing shot vertically up toward the sky like a rocket or meteor, leaving behind no trail and disappearing through a round and curiously regular hole in the clouds before any man could gasp or cry out.
evidence.paraphrase: The colour-entity shoots up into the sky and departs through a hole in the clouds.

evidence.quote: In terms of matter I suppose the thing Ammi described would be called a gas, but this gas obeyed laws that are not of our cosmos.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator classifies the entity as gas-like but notes it obeys laws foreign to our universe.

evidence.quote: It was just a colour out of space\u2014a frightful messenger from unformed realms of infinity beyond all Nature as we know it; from realms whose mere existence stuns the brain and numbs us with the black extra-cosmic gulfs it throws open before our frenzied eyes.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts the entity with everything known in nature, framing it as an alien colour from beyond.

evidence.quote: Five eldritch acres of dusty grey desert remained, nor has anything ever grown there since. To this day it sprawls open to the sky like a great spot eaten by acid in the woods and fields
evidence.paraphrase: The affected land is permanently transformed into a barren grey wasteland where nothing grows.

evidence.quote: Botanists, too, ought to study the stunted flora on the borders of that spot, for they might shed light on the country notion that the blight is spreading\u2014little by little, perhaps an inch a year.
evidence.paraphrase: The blight is said to be slowly spreading outward at about an inch a year.

evidence.quote: And because Ammi recognized that colour, and knew that this last faint remnant must still lurk down there in the well, he has never been quite right since.
evidence.paraphrase: Ammi is permanently psychologically damaged by recognizing the surviving colour in the well.

evidence.quote: the wise men talked of the strange stone's affinity for silicon. It had acted quite unbelievably
evidence.paraphrase: The scientists note the stone's affinity for silicon as an explanation for its behavior.
